title: ChatCompletions compatibility proxy: streaming dechunker + schema bridge
creator: Aisha Bhatt
description:
Goal: Implement a compatibility proxy that reliably maps OpenAI Chat Completions (v1) request/response streams into Redwood's canonical request model and streaming event format. Scope includes: dechunking SSE/delta fragments, reassembling partial 'function_call' payloads, preserving per-delta metadata (role/contentDelta/index), ensuring idempotency and resume semantics for network flaps, and validating structured JSON outputs when clients use `function_call` or expect `json_schema` shaped responses. The adapter should be toggleable per-route (compatibility mode) and include altitude controls for strict vs permissive schema enforcement.

Why: A number of enterprise customers migrate workloads from OpenAI-compatible clients and rely on exact streaming semantics for tool/function invocation. Without a robust bridge we see frequent malformed tool-call reconstructions, duplicate invocation signals, and telemetry gaps. This ticket targets reliability and fidelity improvements while keeping latency overhead minimal.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end tests that replay OpenAI SSE fragments (including out-of-order fragments) and validate reconstructed messages against Redwood canonical shape.
- Streaming dechunker preserves delta ordering and re-emits completed events with stable IDs and an `oa_compat` provenance header.
- Function/tool call reconstruction handles split JSON across multiple deltas, recovers from partial payloads after reconnect, and emits a single `tool_invocation` event.
- Backwards-compatible behavior for non-compat routes (no added latency > 2ms p50).
- Telemetry: per-request mapping latency metric + counters for reconstruction errors and auto-fallbacks.

Implementation notes / design decisions:
- Prototype implemented in Node adapter (spike branch: GH PR #https://github.com/redwood-inference/proxy/pull/3491). The Node version proved reconstruction logic but had GC spikes under high concurrency. We're porting core logic into the runtime-go library to leverage pooled buffers and existing stream parsers.
- Dechunker approach: incremental parser with three states (HEAD, DELTA_ACCUM, FOOTER). Accumulated delta buffers are validated against JSON5 tolerant parser then run through a small sanitizer to drop unknown control tokens. This reduces false-positive malformed calls seen in customer logs.
- Idempotency: use client's `idempotency_key` when available; otherwise generate stable conversation-aware token derived from conversation_id + sequence window; tokens surface to telemetry.
- Security: all reconstructed tool-call payloads pass through KMS-integrated sanitizer when `sensitive=true` label present. Security review required -> tracking in ticket metadata.

Progress updates (chronological):
- 2026-01-15: Spike complete; Node PoC dechunker + unit tests for simple fragments. Notes in design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/oa-cc-compatibility-proxy
- 2026-01-22: Determined Node PoC has memory pressure at 1000 concurrent streams; decision: port to runtime-go for production path, keep Node as shim for local dev.
- 2026-02-05: Prototype runtime-go parser implemented; integration tests added for split function_call JSON across 6 fragments. All tests pass locally. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1776
- 2026-02-18: Load test at staging (5000 qps, 300ms average fragment interval) uncovered increased p99 latency due to sync on schema validation. Mitigation: move strict schema validation to asynchronous phase with a permissive immediate ACK path.
- 2026-03-04: UX/PM review (notes attached) requested a compatibility toggle and audit log entries for every reconstructed tool invocation. Added `compat_mode` per-route flag and audit event emission.
- 2026-03-10: Security review kickoff; awaiting final sign-off on KMS sanitizer flow.

Open review feedback (actionable):
- Add golden files for known broken fragments from customer incident LOG-2026-01-08 (ENG-412587) and assert they do not regress.
- Provide benchmark that isolates schema validation cost; evaluate switching to wasm-based validator for p99 improvements.
- Confirm privacy policy for telemetry keys (remove PII from generated idempotency tokens).

Next steps / remaining work:
- Complete runtime PR reviews and merge parser/transform into runtime-1.19 branch (target: 2026-03-14).
- Add async strict-validator worker + retry semantics for failing validations.
- Wire audit events to console -> rollouts page and ensure they appear in rollout timeline.
- Add e2e migration guide for customers (sample config snippets, compat toggle, expected behavior).

Related artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/oa-cc-compatibility-proxy
- Node PoC PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/proxy/pull/3491
- runtime PR (current): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1776
- Staging load test dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/oa-compat/proxy-load-2026-02

Notes on uniqueness: This ticket focuses on the runtime-focused dechunker + strict/permissive schema bridge and audit/telemetry surfaces rather than purely API translation. That separation reduces blast radius for high-throughput routes and gives customers incremental opt-in to stronger enforcement.
